raw_segments.text: Perched on high stools by the bar, hats shoved back, at the tables calling for more bread
no charge, swilling, wolfing gob-fulls of sloppy food, their eyes bulging, wiping wetted
A pallid suit-faced young man polished his tumbler knife fork and spoon with his napkin.
A man with an infant's saw-sustained napkin tucked round him shoveled gurgling soup down
A man spitting back on his plate, half-masticated gristle, gums, no teeth to choo-choo-choo
Chump-chop from the grill, bolting to get it over, sad boosers eyes, bitten off more
than he can chew, am I like that?
See ourselves as others see us.
Hungry man is an angry man, working tooth and jaw, don't owe a bone.
That last pagan king of Ireland, Cormac in the school-pooim, choked himself at sleddy
St. Patrick converted him to Christianity.
